newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Growth in European electricity demand seen slowing.
newsitem.headline: Growth in European electricity demand seen slowing.

text.p: European electricity demand is expected to increase by 1.7 percent annually between 1995 and 2010, a growth rate which is significantly lower than over the past 25 years, a survey said on Wednesday.

However, the statement from UNIPEDE (International Union of Producers and Distributors of Electrical Energy) and EURELECTRIC (European Grouping of the Electric Supply Industry) said electricity was still projected to increase faster than total final energy, thereby increasing its market share.
In different sectors, the survey said the fastest growth rate was expected for services, with an increase of 2.4 percent annually, followed by transport at 1.6 percent.
At the beginning of 1995, about 42 gigawatts were under construction in the 21 European countries covered by the study.
"The mix of generating capacity will continue to be dominated by conventional thermal power stations, gas-fired plant being the main winner," the statement said.

By the end of this decade, the share of gas-fired plant in the overall net generating capacity will rise to 15 percent. It gave no figure for the current share. It said the extension of nuclear energy over the period 1996-2000 would probably be restricted to France, Finland, the Czech Republic and Slovakia.
